props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant. Defaults to `'bordered'`.

props.name: size
props.description: Trigger size (font + padding). Defaults to `'md'`.

props.name: gap
props.description:
Gap between items → separated "card" look (each item gets its own border +
radius; the outer container chrome is dropped). Omit for the joined default.

props.name: indicatorSide
props.description: Which side the chevron indicator sits on. Defaults to `'right'`.

props.name: actionsWhenClosed
props.description:
Whether `Accordion.Trigger` `actions` stay visible when the item is collapsed.
Defaults to `'show'`; `'hide'` fades them out (and drops them from focus order)
while closed.

props.name: children
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null

props.name: value
props.description:
Controlled open item value. `''` = nothing open (only meaningful when `collapsible`).
Controlled open items array.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description:
Initial open item for uncontrolled use.
Initial open items for uncontrolled use.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description:
Fires when the open item changes.
Fires when the set of open items changes.

props.name: collapsible
props.description:
When true, clicking the currently-open item closes it. Default: `false`
(matches Radix; prevents accidentally closing the only available content).

props.name: tone
props.description: Tone. Defaults to `'info'`. See `AlertTone` for full descriptions.

props.name: title
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description: Optional bold heading. Renders above the description. ReactNode so you can embed inline emphasis (`<>Update 1.2.3 available`). The native HTML `title` attribute (tooltip-on-hover) is collapsed by this prop. Use `aria-label` if you need that.

props.name: children
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description: Description body. Rendered below the title in muted color.

props.name: icon
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description:
Override the tone's default icon. Pass any ReactNode (typically a
lucide-react icon). Pass `null` to hide the icon entirely.

Defaults: `info` → `Info`, `success` → `CheckCircle2`,
`warning` → `AlertTriangle`, `error` → `XCircle`.

props.name: actions
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description:
Optional action row rendered below the description. Typically a single
Button or a Cluster of two ("Retry", "Dismiss"). The component doesn't
manage the action row's layout — pass a pre-laid-out node.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description:
Called when the user clicks the close (×) button. When set, the close
button renders; when omitted, no close button. Alert is **controlled** —
the component does NOT manage internal hidden state. Hide via
conditional render in the consumer:

```tsx
const [show, setShow] = useState(true);
{show && <Alert tone="success" onDismiss={() => setShow(false)}>Saved</Alert>}
```

props.name: topBar
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description:
Top bar slot — sits above the main content, spanning the content column to
the right of the sidebar (not the full window width). Omit for no top bar.

props.name: sidebar
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description:
Sidebar slot — runs the full height down the left, alongside both the top
bar and the content. Sets its own width (intrinsic). Omit for no sidebar.

props.name: sidebarPinned
props.description:
Pin the sidebar to the viewport: `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100dvh`
with internal overflow scrolling. On pages taller than the viewport the
sidebar (and a `Rail` inside it — including its `Rail.Footer` /
CollapseToggle) spans exactly the SCREEN, keeping the footer glued to the
viewport bottom instead of the page bottom. Default `false` (sidebar
stretches to the full row/page height — the original behavior).

Prefer this over wrapping the sidebar slot in `Sticky` — the rail pins its
footer by filling its own `height: 100%` box, which needs a DEFINITE
height to resolve against. `Sticky` sets `align-self: start`, which drops
the row stretch that made it definite, so the footer stops pinning.

`100dvh` is always relative to the real browser viewport, never to a
nested scroll container — so this only pins correctly when AppLayout is
the actual outermost, page-scroll shell (its documented top-level use).
Nest it inside another scrollable region and the sidebar will size to
the whole window, not that region, and overflow it.

props.name: sidebarOverlayBelow
props.description:
Move the sidebar out of the flow and into a left-anchored `<Drawer>` while
the **viewport** is at or below a width threshold: `'sm'` 480px / `'md'`
640px / `'lg'` 768px. Omit for no responsive behavior (the default) — the
sidebar always renders in the flow.

Below the threshold the content column claims the full viewport width, and
the sidebar is reachable only by opening the drawer. Render your own
trigger (a hamburger in the `topBar`) and drive it with `sidebarOpen` +
`onSidebarOpenChange` — AppLayout deliberately renders no trigger of its
own, since where it belongs in the bar is the consumer's call, which means
both props are effectively required together (see `sidebarOpen`'s doc).
Use the exported `useBelowBreakpoint` hook to show that trigger only while
the overlay mode is active.

`sidebarPinned` is ignored below the threshold: the drawer owns the
sidebar's box there, and a `sticky; height: 100dvh` wrapper inside it would
size the rail to the window instead of the drawer.

Measures the viewport (`matchMedia`), not a container — the sidebar's
presence in the row is exactly what the threshold changes, so a container
query would be circular. Same scale and same basis as `<Rail collapseBelow>`.

props.name: sidebarOpen
props.description:
Open state of the overlay sidebar. Technically optional, but effectively
required together with `onSidebarOpenChange` whenever `sidebarOverlayBelow`
is set — AppLayout renders no trigger of its own (see `sidebarOverlayBelow`),
so with both omitted nothing can ever open the drawer; Esc/backdrop close it,
but there's no way in. Has no effect unless `sidebarOverlayBelow` is set and
the viewport is below it.

props.name: onSidebarOpenChange
props.description: Fires whenever the overlay sidebar opens or closes — Esc, backdrop click, swipe, or programmatic. Pair with `sidebarOpen` — see its doc.

props.name: children
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description: Main content slot — fills the remaining space below the top bar.

props.name: name
props.description:
The person's name. Required — used as the `alt`/`aria-label`, as the
source of the initials, and as the seed for the deterministic fallback
color. The same name always renders the same color. When `tooltip` is
true, also used as the tooltip body.

props.name: src
props.description: Image URL. When provided, the `` is rendered with `alt={name}`. Empty/whitespace strings are treated as missing. If the image fails to load (404, network), the component automatically falls back to initials.

props.name: size
props.description:
Diameter.
- `sm` (24px) — table rows, dense lists.
- `md` (32px, default) — most uses.
- `lg` (40px) — detail-page headers.
- `xl` (80px) — member-card popovers / profile headers.

Inside `<AvatarGroup>`, the group's `size` overrides this.

props.name: status
props.description:
Presence dot in the bottom-right.
- `'online'`  — green.
- `'busy'`    — red.
- `'away'`    — amber.
- `'offline'` — gray.
Omit to render no dot at all.

props.name: tooltip
props.description:
Whether to wrap the avatar in a `<Tooltip>` showing `name`. Defaults to
`false` (back-compat — existing renders don't gain a hover affordance).
Inside `<AvatarGroup>`, the group's `tooltip` prop becomes the default
(which itself defaults to `true` for grouped avatars); explicit
per-child still wins.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Semantic tone.
- `neutral` (default) — generic tag, no semantic meaning.
- `info` — new / in-progress / informational states ("Lead", "Pipeline 2026").
- `success` — positive states ("Active", "Won", "Healthy").
- `warning` — at-risk / pending states ("Renewal due", "Pending review").
- `danger` — negative states ("Churned", "Lost", "Blocked").
- `purple` — special / highlighted categories ("Enterprise", "VIP").

props.name: size
props.description:
Pill height and emphasis.
- `md` (20px, default) — the standard "loud label" pill. Uppercase, tracked,
  semibold. Reads as a deliberate status marker.
- `sm` (16px) — quieter inline tag for tight table cells, compact toolbars,
  or anywhere a 20px uppercase pill visually crowds adjacent text. Drops
  the uppercase transform and caps tracking so it sits next to body copy
  without shouting; case is preserved as-typed (write `Active`, get
  `Active`). Same 11px size and semibold weight as `md`.

props.name: dot
props.description:
Render a small filled circle in the badge's text color alongside the
content. Useful when the dot is the primary status signal and the label
is supporting context ("● Active", "Failed ●").
- `start` — dot before the content.
- `end` — dot after the content.

Omit for no dot. The dot is purely decorative (`aria-hidden`) — the badge
text remains the accessible label.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Visual variant.
- `'filled'` (default) — solid tone-tinted pill. The standard "loud status" look.
- `'stripe'` — rectangular block with a tone-colored left stripe + soft tinted body.
  Use for category markers or sidebar labels where pill emphasis is too loud.

props.name: color
props.description:
Optional categorical palette color. When set, takes precedence over
`tone`: the badge fills with the matching `--color-palette-<name>-bg/fg`
tokens. Use for non-semantic categorical labels (e.g., audit event
namespaces, tag colors) where the 6 semantic tones aren't enough.

Both filled and stripe variants are supported; for stripe the
left-border picks up the palette `fg` token.

props.name: align
props.description:
Vertical alignment within the surrounding line of text.
- `baseline` (default) — rides the text baseline; right for body-size text.
- `middle` — centers the badge on the line box; use for a badge inside a
  heading line (`<Title>` / `<PageHeader.Title>`), where baseline riding
  makes the badge look sunken next to large text.

props.name: name
props.description: Which brand mark to render.

props.name: size
props.description: Square pixel size (width = height). Defaults to `20`.

props.name: title
props.description:
Accessible name. Omit (default) for a decorative icon beside a text label —
the icon renders `aria-hidden`. Set it for a standalone icon (e.g. an
icon-only button) → `role="img"` + `aria-label`.

props.name: children
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description:
One or more `<Breadcrumb.Item>` children. The component injects the
separator between items and auto-marks the last child as current
(renders as `<span aria-current="page">` instead of a link).

props.name: separator
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description:
Custom separator between items. Defaults to a small `<ChevronRight>`
lucide icon. The separator renders inside a `<span aria-hidden="true">`
wrapper automatically.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description:
Visible label for the `<nav>` element. Defaults to the i18n value at
`breadcrumb.ariaLabel` (`'Breadcrumb'` in English). Override when
multiple breadcrumb instances coexist on the same page.

props.name: className
props.description: Pass-through className applied to the `<nav>` wrapper.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Visual variant.
- `primary` (default) — the section's main action. Use **one** per page section.
- `secondary` — supporting actions like "Cancel", "Export", "Filter".
- `ghost` — tertiary actions in dense UIs (toolbar buttons, row actions).
- `danger` — destructive operations only (Delete, Revoke, Remove). Pair with a confirmation if irreversible.
- `success` — **transient confirmation only**, not an initial state. Flip to
  `success` for ~1.5s after an action resolves (Save → "Saved!"), then
  flip back. Never render a button as `success` on mount — it has no
  action-intent meaning, only post-action feedback. See the `@example`
  below for the timer pattern.

props.name: size
props.description:
Control height (matches the shared `--size-*` scale used by Input and Avatar).
- `xs` (20px) — icon-only or very dense inline actions (row controls,
  chip-adjacent buttons). Pass `aria-label` when icon-only. Below WCAG
  2.5.5 Level AAA touch-target guidance; reserve for desktop-first surfaces.
- `sm` (24px) — dense toolbars, tables, inline actions.
- `md` (32px, default) — most contexts.
- `lg` (40px) — marketing-style empty states or emphasized primary actions.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description:
Render the button as a square icon-only target — `aspect-ratio` is forced
to 1 so width tracks the size's `height` token (`xs` → 20×20, `sm` → 24×24,
`md` → 32×32, `lg` → 40×40) and `padding` is tightened to a small inset
(4px) so the icon has breathing room without changing the outer shape.

**Always pass `aria-label`** when `iconOnly` is set, otherwise the button
has no accessible name. Pass a single icon as `children`.

Use for inline density (row controls, chip-adjacent actions, toolbar
affordances). For an icon + short text label, leave `iconOnly` off — the
button will lay out as a normal rectangle with the existing gap.

props.name: size
props.description:
Size propagated to children. Per-child `size` (Button or Item) wins
when explicitly set. In visual mode this happens via cloneElement on
Button children. In segmented mode, `<ButtonGroup.Item>` reads from
context.

props.name: disabled
props.description:
Disabled state for the whole group. In segmented mode this is
authoritative (all items become aria-disabled, clicks no-op). In
visual mode this is a no-op — pass `disabled` per `<Button>` instead.

props.name: value
props.description:
Visual mode marker. Never set; absence flips to visual.
Currently-selected item value. Triggers segmented mode.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description:
Fired when a different Item is selected.

Consumers wanting literal-union narrowing can cast the setter:
`onValueChange={(v) => setView(v as 'grid' | 'list')}`.

props.name: aria-label
props.description:
Accessible name for the group landmark. Optional but recommended.
Required in segmented mode (radiogroup needs a label).

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description:
Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
Alternative to aria-label: id of an external labelling element.

props.name: events
props.description: Events to display.

props.name: view
props.description: Active view (controlled). Pair with `onViewChange`.

props.name: defaultView
props.description: Initial view (uncontrolled). Defaults to `'month'`.

props.name: onViewChange
props.description: Fires when the user clicks the view switcher.

props.name: value
props.description: Navigation cursor (controlled).

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial cursor (uncontrolled). Defaults to `new Date()`.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires on prev/next/today/keyboard navigation.

props.name: onDayClick
props.description:
Fires when the user clicks a day cell's empty space.
- Month view: empty space in a day cell, the "+N more" overflow chip, or
  keyboard activation (Enter/Space) on a focused cell.
- Week/Day view: empty hour-grid space inside that day's column —
  **mouse click only**. There is no keyboard equivalent in v3; consumers
  needing keyboard activation in week/day should surface their detail UI
  through the focusable event chips (which fire `onEventClick`).

props.name: onEventClick
props.description: Fires when the user clicks an event chip.

props.name: locale
props.description: Override locale. Defaults to `useLocale()`.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: Override locale-derived first day of week.

props.name: maxLanesPerWeek
props.description: Lane cap per week before "+N more" appears in affected cells (month view). Default 3.

props.name: hourRange
props.description:
Hour range shown in week/day views (inclusive start, exclusive end).
Defaults to `[7, 19]` (7am–7pm). Hours outside this range are NOT
rendered (no row in the grid).

props.name: hourRowHeight
props.description: Pixel height per hour row in week/day views. Default 48.

props.name: renderEvent
props.description:
Optional custom renderer for the inner content of every event chip
across views (month chips, week/day timed blocks, all-day band chips).
The returned ReactNode replaces the default `<time> · <title>` markup
inside the chip's button wrapper — the wrapper still handles tone
background, click, tooltip, and (for timed blocks) absolute positioning.

To override colors, return content with inline styling that fills the
wrapper (e.g., `position: absolute; inset: 0; background: <color>`).

The `ctx` argument carries view-aware metadata: `view`, `asAllDay`,
`continuesLeft`/`continuesRight` (multi-day), `timeLabel`, `duration`.

props.name: padding
props.description:
Inner padding.
- `none` — use when the card contains a table or list that should bleed
  edge-to-edge; inner sections manage their own padding.
- `sm` (12px) — dense info cards.
- `md` (16px) — default for plain-content cards.
- `lg` (24px) — emphasis cards, marketing-style panels.

When omitted, defaults to `'md'` for plain content, or `'none'` when the
card contains compound subcomponents (`Card.Header` / `Card.List` /
`Card.ListRow`) so the header and rows bleed to the card edge automatically.
Pass an explicit value to override the auto-detect.

**Detection is shallow:** only direct children are inspected. Fragments
(`<>...</>`) are transparent — the detection recurses into them, so
conditional renders that wrap compound children in a Fragment still
trigger the auto-detect. But wrapping a `Card.Header` in any other
element (`<div>`, `<Stack>`, etc.) defeats the heuristic — pass
`padding="none"` explicitly in that case.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Optional left-edge tone stripe (3px). Useful for "stat card" / "status card"
patterns where one card in a row needs visual emphasis. Default: no stripe
(the card keeps its standard bordered look).

Uses the same tone vocabulary as `Alert`: `accent` / `info` / `success` /
`warning` / `danger`.

props.name: overflow
props.description:
How the card clips its children at the rounded border.
- `hidden` (default) — children are clipped to the rounded border. This
  prevents the visible seam that appears at the corners when a child has
  square corners (Table's internal scroll wrapper, images, full-bleed
  media). Overlays in this library (DropdownMenu, Tooltip, Popover, Drawer,
  Modal) portal to `document.body` and are NOT clipped by this. Focus
  outlines use CSS `outline`, which is not affected by ancestor overflow.
- `visible` — opt out of clipping. Use when a direct child needs to
  overhang the card edge — decorative badges that protrude from a corner,
  hover-lift transforms whose shadow extends past the card border, etc.

props.name: size
props.description:
Box diameter + label type scale. Defaults to `'md'`.
- `'sm'` — 14px box, font-size-sm label. Dense tables, inline filters.
- `'md'` — 16px box, font-size-md label. Default.
- `'lg'` — 20px box, font-size-lg label. Hero forms, mobile-friendly.

Note: shadows the native HTML `<input size>` attribute (which on
checkboxes is meaningless anyway).

props.name: checked
props.description:
Controlled checked state. Pair with `onChange`. Omit (with optional
`defaultChecked`) for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Initial checked state for uncontrolled use. Defaults to `false`.

props.name: indeterminate
props.description:
Indeterminate (mixed) visual + a11y state. Independent of `checked` —
the box paints with a dash icon and `input.indeterminate = true` so AT
announces "mixed". Consumer drives this based on partial selection
(e.g., a "select all" header where some-but-not-all rows are selected).

When the user clicks an indeterminate checkbox, the native change event
fires with the next `checked` value (`true` if it was `false`). The
consumer typically responds by clearing `indeterminate`.

props.name: label
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description:
Optional label rendered next to the box. The whole `<label>` is the
click target. Omit for icon-only checkboxes (e.g., a DataTable row
selector) — pass `aria-label` instead.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Toggles the error visual + sets `aria-invalid="true"`.

props.name: color
props.description:
Optional palette color for the checked / indeterminate fill. When
set, the filled state uses the palette color's fg token instead
of `--color-accent`. Use to color-tag checkbox groups (per-team,
per-status, per-category). Default unchanged (accent blue).

The focus ring, hover border, and unchecked state remain
accent-colored regardless of `color` — only the checked /
indeterminate fill is affected.

props.name: onChange
props.description:
Fires on every change. Receives the next checked state AND the native
event so consumers can do `event.preventDefault()`, read modifier keys,
etc.

props.name: value
props.description:
Current progress value. Omit (or pass `undefined`) to render the
indeterminate spinning animation.

Two-channel behavior for out-of-range and degenerate values:
- **Visual arc** is clamped to [0%, 100%]. Values outside [0, max]
  render at the nearest valid bound.
- **ARIA `aria-valuenow`** reports the raw number so consumer bugs
  (a value drifting past max) surface in audits and SR announcements.

Degenerate inputs fall back to the indeterminate spinner: `NaN`,
`Infinity`, `-Infinity`, and the case where `max <= 0`. This is the
common file-upload race condition (`bytes_uploaded / total_bytes`
before `total_bytes` is known produces NaN).

props.name: max
props.description:
Upper bound. Defaults to `100`. Consumers using fraction values
(0.0–1.0) pass `max={1}`. Consumers tracking a count ("3 of 10")
pass `max={10}`.

props.name: size
props.description:
Diameter + stroke pairing.
- `sm` — 16px diameter, 2px stroke (inline next to a button — also the
  shape to use for "Saving…" loading affordances; pass no `value` for
  the indeterminate spinner.)
- `md` — 32px diameter, 3px stroke (default — near a heading)
- `lg` — 56px diameter, 4px stroke (page-level loader)

props.name: tone
props.description:
Stroke color tone. Defaults to `'default'` (accent blue). Same vocab
as `<Progress>`. Indeterminate ignores tone — always accent.

props.name: label
props.description:
Optional centered label.
- `false` (default) — no label
- `true` — render `{Math.round(percent)}%` centered. Auto-suppressed
  at `size='sm'` (16px circle has no room for text) AND when
  indeterminate.
- `ReactNode` — render the node centered in BOTH modes. Still
  auto-suppressed at `size='sm'` regardless — the geometry doesn't
  change.

props.name: as
props.description:
Element to render. Defaults to `'div'`.
- `div` (default) — block-level flex container; right for nearly all uses.
- `span` — renders `display: inline-flex`, for phrasing-content contexts
  where a block element is invalid HTML: inside `<button>` (e.g. a
  `ButtonGroup.Item` icon + label), `<a>`, or `<label>`.
- `section` — only for a genuinely standalone, nameable region; pair with
  `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` (an unnamed section is just a div to AT).
- `aside` — exposes a `complementary` landmark to screen readers; label it,
  and never use it for mere visual grouping.

`span` is the ONLY value valid inside `<button>`/`<a>`/`<label>` —
`section` and `aside` are flow content and remain invalid HTML there.

props.name: gap
props.description:
Gap between children, in pixels:
`xs` (4) / `sm` (8) / `md` (12, default) / `lg` (16) / `xl` (24) / `2xl` (32).

props.name: justify
props.description:
Horizontal distribution.
- `start` (default) — items at the start.
- `center` — items centered.
- `end` — items at the end. Canonical form-footer pattern.
- `between` — first item at start, last at end, gap between. Canonical toolbar pattern (title left, actions right).

props.name: align
props.description:
Vertical alignment.
- `start` / `center` (default) / `end` / `baseline`.

props.name: wrap
props.description:
Whether children wrap to additional lines when the container is narrow.
- `true` (default) — natural for toolbars and tag lists.
- `false` — use sparingly, when overflow is preferable to wrapping
  (e.g. inside a narrow table cell with fixed-width action buttons).

props.name: tone
props.description:
Color tone for the code text. The chip background stays the same;
only the text color changes.
- `default` — `--color-fg`
- `muted` — `--color-fg-muted`
- `accent` — `--color-accent`
- `danger` — `--color-danger`

props.name: children
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description: Code content.

props.name: value
props.description: Current color as `#RRGGBB`. Controlled — required.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires per drag tick + on input change + on preset click. High frequency during drags.

props.name: onChangeEnd
props.description: Fires on the trailing edge of an interaction. Use for commit-style logic.

props.name: presets
props.description:
Optional preset color swatches. If provided, rendered as a grid below
the hue slider in the panel.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable interaction. Trigger doesn't open; panel is non-interactive.

props.name: triggerLabel
props.description:
Accessible label for the default trigger. Defaults to the i18n value at
`colorPicker.triggerLabel` (`'Pick a color'` in English). Ignored when
a custom trigger is provided via `<ColorPicker.Trigger>`.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description:
Id(s) of element(s) that label the trigger button. Forwarded onto the
focusable trigger (not the root wrapper) and takes precedence over the
generated `aria-label`. Set automatically when wrapped in `<Field label>`.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description:
Id(s) of element(s) that describe the trigger button (e.g. a Field error or
helper text). Forwarded onto the focusable trigger, not the root wrapper.

props.name: popoverPlacement
props.description: Popover placement (split internally into side + align). Default `'bottom-start'`.

props.name: children
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description: Optional `<ColorPicker.Trigger asChild>` override for custom triggers.

props.name: children
props.description:
The trigger element. Same forwardRef-required contract as
`<Popover.Trigger>` — `<Button>` qualifies; a custom component without
`forwardRef` does not.

props.name: title
props.description:
Heading text. Renders inside `<Popover.Heading>` (an `<h3>`) and wires
`aria-labelledby` on the dialog automatically.

props.name: description
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description:
Optional body text below the title. When provided, wires
`aria-describedby` so screen readers announce it.

props.name: confirmLabel
props.description:
Confirm button label. Defaults to the i18n value at
`confirmationPopover.confirm` (`'Confirm'` in English).

props.name: variant
props.description: `'danger'` makes Confirm a danger-variant button. Defaults to `'default'` (primary).

props.name: onConfirm
props.description:
Async-aware confirm handler. May return a Promise; while pending,
both buttons disable, the Confirm button shows a small spinner, and
Escape / click-outside dismissal is blocked.

- Resolve → popover closes.
- Reject → popover stays open, buttons re-enable. `onCancel` is NOT
  fired (the user neither confirmed nor cancelled — it's an error
  state owned by the consumer).

The consumer is expected to surface error feedback externally (toast,
inline message, etc.). ConfirmationPopover does NOT render errors.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: Optional. Fires on Cancel click, Escape, or click-outside dismissal. NOT fired if `onConfirm` rejects.

props.name: initialFocusRef
props.description:
Direct initial focus into the panel's content instead of the default
Cancel button — e.g. an `<Input>` rendered in `description` for a rename
flow. When provided and its `.current` is non-null on open, the component
focuses this element after the panel mounts (skipping the Cancel-focus).
Tip: add `onFocus={(e) => e.currentTarget.select()}` to a text input to
select its contents so the user can type/replace immediately.

props.name: side
props.description: Preferred side. Default `'top'` — confirmations anchor above the trigger by convention.

props.name: align
props.description: Edge alignment. Default `'center'`.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description: Gap in px between trigger and panel. Default `10`.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Open-change callback. Required when `open` is provided.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Default open state for uncontrolled usage. Defaults to `false`.

props.name: width
props.description: Fixed width — a named step (`xs`–`xl`) or `'full'` (100%).

props.name: minWidth
props.description: Minimum width floor — a named step or `'full'` (100%).

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum width cap — the common case (e.g. a search input at `'sm'`).

props.name: flex
props.description:
Flex behavior as a child of a flex row/column.
- `'grow'` — fill remaining space (`flex: 1 1 0`) and shrink below content
  width (`min-width: 0`) so a truncating child (`<Text truncate>`) can clip.
- `'auto'` — size to content, may grow/shrink (`flex: 1 1 auto`).
- `'shrink'` — don't grow, may shrink (`flex: 0 1 auto`, the flex default).
- `'none'` — fixed, never grow/shrink (`flex: 0 0 auto`).

props.name: children
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description: The content to size. Required — a Constrain with nothing inside has nothing to constrain.

props.name: hasPrevious
props.description:
Whether a previous page exists. When `false`, the previous button is
rendered as `disabled` (layout stays stable; consumer doesn't have to
conditionally hide it).

props.name: hasNext
props.description: Whether a next page exists.

props.name: onPrevious
props.description: Called when the user clicks previous (not fired when disabled).

props.name: onNext
props.description: Called when the user clicks next (not fired when disabled).

props.name: previousLabel
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description:
Label for the previous button. Defaults to the i18n value at
`pagination.previous` (`'Previous'` in English). Override for domain
phrasing (`'Newer'` in a reverse-chronological feed).

props.name: nextLabel
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description:
Label for the next button. Defaults to the i18n value at
`pagination.next` (`'Next'` in English).

props.name: size
props.description:
Visual size — `'sm'` / `'md'` (default) / `'lg'`. Shares the
`<Pagination>` size scale so the two components match when used
alongside each other.

props.name: disabled
props.description: When `true`, both buttons are disabled regardless of has-prev/-next.

props.name: aria-label
props.description:
Accessible name for the wrapper `<nav>`. Defaults to the i18n value at
`pagination.ariaLabel` (`'Pagination'` in English).

props.name: value
props.description:
The controlled layout: top-level items plus an ordered array of
collapsible sections. `DashboardCanvas` never mutates this value — every
change flows out through `onChange`.

props.name: onChange
props.description:
Fires once per completed gesture — a drop, a resize end, a collapse
toggle, a section reorder, or a cross-container move — with the whole
next `value`. Omit for a read-only or fully static canvas; without it,
drags preview live but nothing persists on drop.

props.name: renderItem
props.description:
Renders the body of an item by id. Called for every item on every
render — including items inside a COLLAPSED section (its body stays
mounted and `inert`, not unmounted, so Accordion's own collapse
animation has real content to animate) — and once more for the dragged
item mid-gesture (the cursor-following ghost). Keep it pure; a widget
that fetches on mount pays that cost even while its section is
collapsed. The cell itself is a bare positioned box with no
background/border/radius/shadow of its own and no minimum height beyond
its `h` row-span — that chrome belongs here, in whatever this returns
(typically a `<Card>`); size the content to the cell, or accept that a
shorter widget in a taller cell shows bare (dotted, in edit mode) space
below it.

props.name: renderSectionHeader
props.description:
Optional extra controls in a section's header (a title editor, a
`DropdownMenu` trigger) rendered by section id, to the right of the
title. Keep it small — the header row is not a general-purpose toolbar.
Pointer presses inside the slot never start a band-reorder drag.

props.name: constraints
props.description: Per-item size constraints, consulted when clamping resize gestures.

props.name: columns
props.description:
Column count of every container grid (top level and each section's
sub-grid). All placement/resize bounds clamp against it. Minimum 1;
fractional or sub-1 values are the consumer's bug, not validated.

Layouts are NOT converted between column counts — a `value` saved at one
`columns` renders at half width when the count doubles. Schemas written
for the pre-#350 12-column grid (e.g. the eocrm layout-v2 spec) either
pass `columns={12}` to match, or migrate their saved placements to 24.

props.name: stackBelow
props.description:
Container width at (inclusive) and below which every container grid
re-templates to one column and pointer + keyboard editing turns off:
`sm` 480px / `md` 640px / `lg` 768px, measured against the canvas's OWN
width (container query), not the viewport. Section collapse toggles keep
working at any width.

props.name: readOnly
props.description:
View-only mode: identical geometry, but no drag/resize wiring, no resize
handles, and no keyboard editing — the canvas renders `value` and lets
section collapse toggles keep working. The canvas also disables editing
on its own, without this prop, once its own width drops to or below the
`stackBelow` breakpoint (single-column stack) — `readOnly` is for a
consumer-chosen view mode, the width gate is automatic.

props.name: hover
props.description: Hover highlight on body rows. Defaults TRUE (DataTable rows are usually interactive).

props.name: loadingRowCount
props.description: Number of skeleton rows when `loading`. Defaults 10.

props.name: emptyState
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description: Element shown when `data` is empty and not loading. Defaults to a stock <EmptyState>.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Required for a11y when no caption is provided.

props.name: caption
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null

props.name: dragWholeColumn
props.description:
Drag the whole column while reordering, not just its header cell.

Default `true` — the dragged column's body cells travel with its header,
and every column the drag displaces shifts its body cells too, so the
header row and the body never disagree mid-drag. Costs one CSS-variable
write per shifted column per frame; the cells move on the compositor, so
the table body is not re-rendered during pointer movement. It does cost
two full body reconciliations per drag — one at drag start, one at drag
end — because the drag-active flag is component state and body rows are
not memoized; that is the number to weigh for a very large table.

Set `false` for the cheaper preview: only the dragged header cell follows
the pointer and the body stays put until drop. Worth it for very large
tables on low-end hardware, or to restore the previous behavior.

Pinned columns never move under either setting — they are excluded from
reordering entirely.

The two settings also differ on **what a release means when no unpinned
slot is under the column** — over a pinned column, or off the table
entirely. Default: the drop commits the slot the preview is showing. The
opt-out: the drop is discarded, because dnd-kit's own preview retracts (the
header snaps back home) in that situation, and a commit would contradict
it. See the component's `@remarks`.

props.name: value
props.description: Selected date. `null` = no value. Pair with `onChange` for controlled use.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial selected date for uncontrolled use.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires when the value changes.

props.name: locale
props.description: Override locale (otherwise reads `useLocale()`).

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest selectable date (inclusive).

props.name: max
props.description: Latest selectable date (inclusive).

props.name: isDateDisabled
props.description: Per-date disable callback.

props.name: clearable
props.description: Show the ✕ clear button when a value is set. Defaults to `true`.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Toggle red border + focus ring + `aria-invalid="true"`.

props.name: name
props.description: Form name. When set, renders a hidden mirror `<input>` with the ISO date.

props.name: size
props.description:
Field height + type scale. Same scale as `<Input>`. Defaults to `'md'`.
Affects only the trigger row; the popover month grid is fixed-size.

- `'sm'` — 24px tall.
- `'md'` — 32px tall (default).
- `'lg'` — 40px tall.

props.name: granularity
props.description:
Picker precision.

- `'day'` (default) — date only; behavior unchanged from prior releases.
- `'minute'` — adds a manual-entry time input below the calendar grid.
  The trigger text shows `HH:mm` after the date. The hidden form mirror
  (when `name` is set) emits ISO local datetime (`2026-05-28T14:30`).

Time is preserved across date re-picks. Picking from a `null` value
defaults the time to `00:00`.

props.name: timeStep
props.description:
Minutes step for the `<TimeField>` popover and for rounding typed
time input on commit. Defaults to `15`. Set `1` to disable rounding.
Only meaningful when `granularity='minute'`.

props.name: hourCycle
props.description:
Display cycle for the embedded `<TimeField>` + the trigger's time tail.

- `'24'` — `"HH:mm"` in the trigger; 24h hour list in the time popover.
- `'12'` — `"h:mm AM/PM"` in the trigger; 12h hour list + AM/PM column.
- `'auto'` (default) — derives from the active locale via Intl. en-US →
  `'12'`; ru-RU / de-DE / fr-FR → `'24'`.

Only meaningful when `granularity='minute'`. Typed input is lenient
regardless of cycle — both `"14:30"` and `"2:30 PM"` parse on blur.

props.name: value
props.description: Selected range. `null` = no range. Pair with `onChange` for controlled use.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial range for uncontrolled use.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires when a complete range commits (after second click in grid, or successful typed parse on blur).

props.name: locale
props.description: Override locale (otherwise reads `useLocale()`).

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest selectable date (inclusive). Both halves and typed input are gated.

props.name: max
props.description: Latest selectable date (inclusive).

props.name: isDateDisabled
props.description: Per-date disable predicate.

props.name: size
props.description:
Field height + type scale. Same scale as `<DatePicker>`. Defaults to `'md'`.
Affects only the trigger row; the two-month popover grid is fixed-size.

- `'sm'` — 24px tall.
- `'md'` — 32px tall (default).
- `'lg'` — 40px tall.

props.name: clearable
props.description: Show the ✕ clear button when a range is set. Defaults to `true`.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Toggle red border + focus ring + `aria-invalid="true"`.

props.name: nameStart
props.description: Form name for the START half (hidden `<input>`).

props.name: nameEnd
props.description: Form name for the END half.

props.name: granularity
props.description:
Picker precision.

- `'day'` (default) — date only; behavior unchanged from prior releases.
- `'minute'` — adds two manual-entry time inputs (start + end) below
  the two-month grid. The trigger text shows `HH:mm` after each date.
  Hidden form mirrors (when `nameStart` / `nameEnd` are set) emit ISO
  local datetime (`2026-05-28T14:30`).

At `'minute'` the start/end time inputs are shown and editable in the
popover even before a range is picked (defaulting to `00:00` / `23:59`).
Times entered in the empty state are applied when the range is committed
(instead of the bare defaults), and existing times are preserved across
date re-picks. Same-day ranges with end-time < start-time are silently
clamped so end-time ≥ start-time.

props.name: timeStep
props.description:
Minutes step for the start + end `<TimeField>` popovers and for
rounding typed time input on commit. Defaults to `15`. Set `1` to
disable rounding. Only meaningful when `granularity='minute'`.

props.name: hourCycle
props.description:
Display cycle for the two embedded `<TimeField>`s + the trigger's
time tails.

- `'24'` — `"HH:mm"` in trigger + 24h hour lists in popovers.
- `'12'` — `"h:mm AM/PM"` in trigger + 12h hour lists + AM/PM column.
- `'auto'` (default) — derives from the active locale via Intl. en-US →
  `'12'`; ru-RU → `'24'`.

Only meaningful when `granularity='minute'`. Typed input is lenient
regardless of cycle — both `"14:30"` and `"2:30 PM"` parse on blur.

props.name: termWidth

CSS length applied to the term column in horizontal layout (e.g. `'180px'`,
`'20%'`, `'max-content'`). Default `'max-content'` — column sizes to the
longest term across all rows. Set explicitly when you need consistent
alignment across multiple DefinitionLists on the same screen.

props.name: spacing
props.description: Vertical padding per item. See `DefinitionListSpacing`. Default `'sm'`.

props.name: dividers
props.description:
Render a 1px border between items. Default `false` (clean, dense look).
Set when migrating from a `Card.List` and you want to preserve the
table-row separator visual.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout direction. Defaults to `'horizontal'`.

props.name: variant
props.description: Line style. Defaults to `'solid'`.

props.name: size
props.description: Line thickness tier. Defaults to `'sm'`.

props.name: children
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description:
Optional centered label rendered between two line segments.
Common pattern: `<Divider>OR</Divider>` for auth-form section breaks.

When `children` is set, the root becomes `<div role="separator">`
instead of `<hr>` (HTML `<hr>` cannot have children).

Works with `orientation="vertical"` but renders awkwardly (text wraps
across two short line segments). Avoid vertical + label combos.

One of the 30 `PaletteColor`s — renders the bare circle in that color's
saturated `--color-palette-<name>-fg` token. Takes precedence over `tone`.

props.name: tone

A semantic `BadgeTone` (`neutral` default / `info` / `success` / `warning` /
`danger` / `purple`) — used when `color` is omitted.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. Required — Drawer has no uncontrolled mode.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fired when Drawer wants to change open state — Esc, overlay click, Close, swipe, programmatic.

props.name: side
props.description: Edge the drawer slides in from. Defaults to 'right'.

props.name: size
props.description: Size preset. Width for left/right, height for top/bottom. Defaults to 'md'.

props.name: overlay
props.description: Overlay variant. 'solid' (default) | 'blur'.

props.name: stackMode
props.description:
How this drawer relates to other open overlays (Modals or Drawers).
'overlay' (default): parent stays visible. 'replace': parent hidden via display:none.

props.name: disableEscapeClose
props.description: Disable Escape-to-close. Default false.

props.name: dismissOnOverlayClick
props.description: When false, overlay click does NOT close. Default true.

props.name: dragToClose
props.description: Enable swipe-to-close gesture on touch devices (from Header). Default true.

props.name: initialFocusRef
props.description: Initial focus target on open.

Fired with the chosen emoji character (e.g. `'👍'`) when the user clicks a
cell or presses Enter/Space on a focused cell. This is the picker's single
output — wire it to insert into an editor, set a reaction, etc.

props.name: recent

Recently-used emoji characters (e.g. `['👍', '🎉', '❤️']`), most-recent first.
When provided, a "Recently used" section renders at the top of the grid (only
while not searching). The consumer owns persistence — keep the list yourself
(e.g. in localStorage), update it in `onSelect`, and pass it back. Duplicates
are de-duped; a char outside the curated set still renders (labelled by the
char). Omit or pass `[]` for no recent section.

props.description:
Required title. Rendered as a semantic heading (default `

`). Accepts ReactNode so inline emphasis works (e.g., `<>Found 0 results`). Keep it short and announceable — AT users hear it via heading navigation.

props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description: Optional description rendered below the title.

props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description:
Optional action(s) rendered below the description. Typically a
`<Button>` or a `<Cluster gap="sm">` of buttons.

props.name: size
props.description:
Visual size. Defaults to `'md'`.
- `'sm'` — compact for inline / popover use (empty Select results,
  empty filter chips). Icon target 24px, font-size-sm title.
- `'md'` — default for cards / sections (DataTable empty row, inbox
  empty). Icon target 32px, font-size-md title.
- `'lg'` — hero / full-page empty states. Icon target 48px,
  font-size-xl title.

props.name: align
props.description:
Horizontal alignment of the stacked content. Defaults to `'center'`.
Use `'start'` when the empty state sits in a tight column where
centering would look stranded.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description:
Heading level for the `title`. Defaults to `3` (renders `<h3>`).
Set higher (4–6) when the empty state lives deep inside the page's
heading hierarchy. Set to `2` when the empty state IS the page's
primary content. Values outside `1–6` clamp to `3`.

props.name: icon
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description: Leading icon — consumer passes the element (e.g. a lucide icon). Rendered aria-hidden.

props.name: label
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description:
Entity name. Optional at the type level only to satisfy the polymorphic
`forwardRef` generic (same workaround `<Rail.Item>` documents on its
`children`); in practice every chip needs a label.

props.name: prefix
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description: Muted leading run before the name (e.g. task key `ENG-5`).

props.name: status
props.description: Inline workflow status, separated by a small dot and rendered in the status's own color.

props.name: color
props.description:
Optional categorical palette color for the chip fill. When set, takes
precedence over the default accent chip tokens: the chip fills with the
matching `--color-palette-<name>-bg/-fg` pair (same contract as `Badge
color` — picking a readable pair is the consumer's call). Omit for the
default fill, which matches RichText's `@mention` styling
(`--color-accent-bg-subtle` / `--color-accent`) so a chip and a rendered
mention read as the same visual object. The `status` run keeps its own
resolved color independent of this prop, and `unavailable` still mutes
the label/status text over any `color`.

props.name: href
props.description: Renders `as="a"` with this href when `as` is omitted.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Loading placeholder: icon slot + `…` body, aria-busy; the label stays in
the DOM visually hidden so the chip keeps its accessible name. Purely
visual — with a link target (`href`/`as`) the chip stays a live,
keyboard-reachable link while loading.

props.name: unavailable
props.description:
Entity missing/no access: muted styling. With a link target (`href`/`as`)
the chip remains a real link — unavailable is a visual state, not a
disabling one. Only a target-less chip (bare span) becomes non-interactive
with aria-disabled.

props.description:
Icon rendered above the title. Pass a lucide icon (sized by the consumer —
lg=48, md=32, sm=24), custom SVG, or any ReactNode. The icon's color is set
by `tone`; pass `aria-hidden="true"` on it when purely decorative.

props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<AwaitedReactNode> | null
props.description:
Required title, rendered as a semantic heading (default `<h1>` — it's
usually the page heading). Accepts ReactNode for inline emphasis.
